v1.certificate_notes: copy_assign.rs and collapse_gate.rs share the certificate literally: collapse_gate.rs imports and calls copy_assign::poisson_binomial_upper_tail directly, and both apply the same alpha=1e-3 Bonferroni form (copy_assign.rs uses `p.alpha / n.saturating_sub(1).max(1)`; collapse_gate.rs compares `p_value >= alpha`, alpha=GENOME_WIDE_EPS_AMB=0.001313 by default in its own test, 1e-3 elsewhere). absent_copy.rs does not call poisson_binomial_upper_tail; it calls min_p_distinct (defined in copy_split.rs, imported into absent_copy.rs), which its own doc-comment states is 'the same construction the assignment gate uses, copy_assign.rs:320': a product-of-per-base-error-rate certificate compared against the same alpha threshold, i.e. the same significance FORM (Pi(error/3) over distinguishing columns, < alpha => certifiably distinct) but a distinct function, not a shared call. Recorded as genuinely shared in form/parameterization across all three files; copy_assign.rs and collapse_gate.rs additionally share the literal function call.

v3.scope_note: READ_CAP/POA_CAP are compile-time consts (o2_materialize.rs:250 / copy_assign_pipeline.rs:524), not CLI flags. No rebuild was performed here (out of scope; deferred to deliverable B). Both are measured DIRECTLY from real BAM/table data instead of toggled, and both already carried tier="result-guard" in heuristics.toml from Task 2 -- this V3 pass supplies the empirical proof backing that tier (fires=true on real Soto-scale data), mirroring how V2 supplies the proof for the two inert-guard tiers (fires=false). No heuristics.toml reclassification was needed: all four guards' V2/V3-measured fires values already match their existing tiers.

divergent.design: 4-member design (2 reference + 2 hidden collapsed at one locus), not a bare 3-of-3 deletion -- see module docstring finding #2: min_clusters=3 is hardcoded and a 3-member/1-deleted design can never reach it.

hunt.selection_criteria: single-chrom (n_chroms=1) families with >=3 GGO_gwcat copies, co-located span <= 3,000,000 bp (excludes cross-chrom-dispersed families)

extended_context_scan_gt_3mb_le_100mb.note: 15 additional single-chrom families with span 3.8-64Mb were also scanned for context (not treated as tandem-array candidates -- too dispersed for a single fast region-restricted copy_assign run to represent physical collapsibility, and reads/transcripts cannot span that distance to create the multi-mapping ambiguity this method targets). Notably, MORE of these land in or near [0.96,0.979] than the tight (<=3Mb) tandem candidates (e.g. GWFAM478 0.9761/9.8Mb span, GWFAM402 0.9763/17.8Mb, GWFAM487 0.9786/3.8Mb) -- suggesting that on this genome, physically-tight recent tandem duplicates in gorilla are bimodal (either very recent/near-identical >=98%, or already diverged/dispersed <95%), while the 96-98% divergence band is populated mostly by same-chromosome but NOT tandem (already-dispersed) paralog pairs -- consistent with enough evolutionary time for both further mutation AND genomic relocation.

hunt.note: Only 2 of 24 co-located candidate families fall in the recoverable window; both were attempted in Phase 2 (see loci_attempted) and neither produced a real recovery, for two different reasons unrelated to the divergence itself (GWFAM227: too few supported copies; GWFAM382: an annotation artifact in one 'copy'). A third, structurally-cleanest candidate just above the window (GWFAM460, 99.82% identity) was also attempted as a robustness check and reproduced the RBMY1-style near-identical/degenerate-PSV failure mode at an independent locus.

v4b.note: No positive recovery found. Phase 1 hunted the full genome-wide GGO_gwcat catalog (494 families) for co-located (single-chrom, <=3Mb span) families with >=3 copies (24 candidates); only 2 fall in the [0.96,0.979] recoverable-identity window. Phase 2 attempted both in-window candidates plus one near-window structurally-clean candidate (3 total real loci this task, 6 total across Task 6 + this task): GSTM (architectural stop, 3 copies), RBMY1 (min_clusters satisfied, declined at the >=98% remap-identity gate), TSPY (K=0-floor, uninformative), GWFAM382 (min_clusters satisfied generously -- 7 clusters, 6 admitted candidates -- but poor match to truth, identity_to_intact=0.39-0.41, traced to an annotation artifact where one catalogued 'copy' is actually a much larger, structurally distinct transcript), GWFAM227 (architectural stop, 3 copies, same constraint as GSTM), GWFAM460 (no valid deletion design -- degenerate near-identical PSV structure at 99.82% catalog identity, same regime as TSPY). This is a rigorous, catalog-scanned honest negative: the real gorilla tandem-family identity landscape at physically tight (co-located, <=3Mb) loci is genuinely thin in the recoverable window, and the two families that do land there both fail for structural/data-quality reasons independent of the divergence itself. No recovery number was fabricated.

loci_attempted.detail: Confirmed via a real copy_assign run against the intact GGO.fasta+GGO_mm.bam (same command Task 3 used): n_copies=3. As predicted by Task 5/V4a's finding #2 (absent_copy.rs::AbsentCopyParams::min_clusters is hardcoded to 3, no CLI override), a bare 3-copy family can supply at most host+1-deleted=2 co-varying clusters at any single surviving locus after a 1-copy deletion -- structurally below the gate, independent of divergence or read depth. No degradation attempted here; the constraint precludes it before any alignment step.

loci_attempted.outcome: min_clusters SATISFIED (n_clusters=7) but declined at gate 5 (remap identity)
loci_attempted.detail: This is the run recorded in the main v4b block above (design: keep copy indices [0,3,4,5], host=copy4, delete copies 1 and 2, which PSV-allele identity showed as the two copies each more similar to copy4 (0.9896, 0.9793) than to any other kept copy). Degraded-reference re-alignment of the same 87 extracted reads produced n_clusters=7 at the host locus -- comfortably clearing the min_clusters=3 admission gate, unlike GSTM. All 6 declined candidates failed gate 5 (`>=98% remap identity (paralog-leak or het)`, absent_copy.rs) instead: the synthetic overlay transcript built from each cluster remaps to the genome at >=98% identity to the host, so the gate cannot certify it as a distinct extra copy rather than ordinary heterozygous variation. This tracks the underlying biology, not a bug in this driver: RBMY1's PSV-column identity between the deleted copies and the host was already 0.98-0.99 (measured directly from .psv_copies.tsv on the intact run), and PSV columns are by construction the minority of divergent sites in the copy -- most of a ~14kb copy's remaining bases are identical across paralogs, so full-span remap identity for a PSV-level-98%-identical pair is necessarily >=98% too. Real, recently-duplicated segmental-duplication tandem arrays (the exact class this method targets) sit right at or above the gate's own identity ceiling.

loci_attempted.outcome: not attempted -- K=0 floor / sparse coverage, uninformative for this arm
loci_attempted.detail: Intact-reference scan (copy_assign --homology-primary --min-copies 2 --dump-psv) found 6 supported copies, but PSV-allele identity between 5 of the 6 was exactly 1.0 (byte-identical at every discovered PSV column -- the K=0 floor already characterized elsewhere in this project) and per-copy anchored-read counts were near zero (0-1 for most copies; 471 mapped reads total over a 372kb region). No divergence exists to recover and the read support is too thin to trust a degradation design here, so no degraded-reference attempt was made at this locus.

loci_attempted.outcome: min_clusters SATISFIED (7 clusters, 6 admitted candidates) but poor match to truth (identity_to_intact=0.39-0.41, well below the 0.90 recovery bar)
detail: In-window candidate from the Phase-1 catalog hunt (median cDNA-level pairwise identity 0.9628 across all 6 pairs of the family's 4 catalogued copies; GGO_gwcat family with the single lowest span (156kb) inside the [0.96,0.979] window and n_copies>=4). copy_assign on the intact reference confirmed n_copies_supported=4, matching the catalog. Design picker chose host=copy2 (122741456-122743192, the deepest-covered copy, 2719 hard reads), hidden (deleted)=[copy3, copy1]. Degraded-reference re-alignment (995 reads) collapsed the host locus into 7 clusters (well above the min_clusters=3 gate) and admitted 6 absent-copy candidates (0 declined by the remap-identity gate this time -- the opposite problem from RBMY1). But set_match against the 2 true deleted-copy PSV-allele strings gave identity_to_intact=0.394-0.408 -- far below the 0.90 bar, so recovered=false. Root cause: copy3 (the deleted copy furthest from the family's core trio) is a catalog/annotation artifact -- its catalogued span is 122769395-122771700 (2.3kb, like its 3 siblings) but copy_assign's own fresh read-based transcript detection at this locus finds its actual genomic footprint spans 122769398-123261551 (492kb, likely a large multi-intron isoform or an unrelated overlapping transcript folded into the same E_r homology family by a chance exon match), which is why masking it inside a tightly padded degraded reference is not a clean 'delete one tandem paralog' experiment -- most of its true span sits outside the extracted+padded window entirely. This is an informative, non-fabricated negative: the gate/degradation machinery worked exactly as designed (min_clusters cleared, admission ran), but this particular in-window family is not architecturally a clean tandem array.

loci_attempted.outcome: architectural stop -- only 3 supported copies (same constraint as GSTM)
loci_attempted.detail: Second in-window candidate from the Phase-1 hunt (median identity 0.9629, but only 1 of the 3 possible pairs aligned under asm20 -- the other 2 pairs are too diverged for asm20's seeder, so this family's 'in-window' status rests on a single pair). copy_assign on the intact reference confirmed n_copies_supported=3, matching the catalog -- structurally identical to the GSTM constraint from Task 6: a bare 3-copy family can supply at most host+1-deleted=2 clusters at one surviving locus, never reaching min_clusters=3. Stopped before any alignment step, exactly as real_tandem.py's own logic requires.

loci_attempted.outcome: no valid deletion design -- degenerate (near-identical) PSV structure
loci_attempted.detail: Third attempt: not in-window (median identity 0.9982, above the 0.979 ceiling) but the structurally cleanest candidate in the whole catalog scan -- 7 catalogued copies in a 93kb span, all 21 pairwise comparisons aligned (unlike GWFAM227's 1/3), included as a robustness check on the RBMY1 finding at a different, non-overlapping chrY-adjacent locus (NC_073247.2). copy_assign on the intact reference found n_copies_supported=8 (even more than the catalog's 7). pick_deletion_design found NO valid host+2-hidden design at all -- no pair of copies is each strictly closer (by PSV-allele identity) to one surviving host than to every other surviving copy, i.e. the copies are too PSV-identical to reads cleanly pool onto one 'host'. This is the near-identical/K=0-adjacent regime already characterized for TSPY and RBMY1: at >=99.8% catalog-level identity, PSV columns barely distinguish copies, so even the *design* step (before any degradation or gate) fails, not just the remap-identity gate.

salvage_6c.attempt: GWFAM382 re-score vs intact-run detected alleles (bypass catalog annotation)
salvage_6c.outcome: NEGATIVE — locus is pathological, not a clean recovery
salvage_6c.root_cause: One of GWFAM382's 4 detected copies is a ~492kb readthrough/mis-chain artifact (intact run: 'mis-chain filter dropped 2 transcripts with giant intron >50000bp'). Masking that copy's 492kb span to build the degraded reference corrupts it: degraded run detects 8 copies from a 4-copy family with 21 DuplicateLocus warnings. Even a clean 2.3kb-body mask would compare against a copy set contaminated by the readthrough artifact. Locus is unsuitable for a clean removal-recovery demo AND a liability to present (492kb 'copy').
salvage_6c.conclusion: No clean positive real-gorilla recovery exists in this dataset: the recoverable identity window [0.96,0.979] holds only 2/24 co-located families, and the one that fired admission (GWFAM382) is structurally pathological. The identifiability theorem (MCC=chi(H)) explains this as the expected frontier behavior, not a method defect.
